st: Rinse the bulgur, cover with water for 15 minutes, then drain and squeeze dry.

Make the filling: heat [[2 tbsp]] oil, cook the diced onion for 4 minutes, add [[0.5 lb]] lamb and cook 6 minutes until no pink remains (160°F/71°C). Stir in the pine nuts, [[0.5 tsp]] allspice, [[0.5 tsp]] salt and the cinnamon. Cool completely.

For the shell, pulse the grated onion, [[1 lb]] raw lamb, bulgur, [[1 tsp]] allspice, [[1.5 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper in a food processor, adding ice water a spoonful at a time, until a smooth paste forms.
Chill the shell mixture for 30 minutes so it is easy to shape.
Wet your hands. Take a lemon-sized ball of shell mixture, poke a hole with your finger and press the wall thin into a cup shape.
Put a spoonful of filling inside, pinch the top closed and shape into an oval with pointed ends.
Heat [[3 cup]] oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C). Fry 3 or 4 kibbeh at a time for 5 minutes until dark brown and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with yogurt or lemon.
Mix [[0.25 cup]] yogurt, [[4 clove]] garlic, [[2 tbsp]] lemon juice, [[2 tsp]] cumin, [[2 tsp]] paprika, [[0.5 tsp]] cinnamon, [[0.5 tsp]] turmeric and [[1 tsp]] salt in a large bowl.
Add the chicken, coat well, cover and marinate in the fridge for 6 hours.
Make the garlic sauce: stir [[0.25 cup]] yogurt, [[2 clove]] garlic, [[3 tbsp]] tahini, [[1 tbsp]] lemon juice and [[0.5 tsp]] salt together. Chill.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Cook the chicken for 6 minutes per side until deeply browned and 165°F (74°C) inside. Work in batches.
Rest the chicken for 5 minutes and slice thinly.
Warm the pita, spread with garlic sauce, add chicken and pickles, and roll tight. Toast in a dry pan for a minute if you like.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the pita pieces with [[1 tbsp]] olive oil on a baking sheet.
Bake for 8 minutes until golden and crisp, then cool.
Whisk [[3 tbsp]] lemon juice, [[0.25 cup]] olive oil, the garlic, [[2 tsp]] sumac and [[0.75 tsp]] salt in a small bowl.
Put the lettuce, tomatoes, cucumbers, radishes, scallions and mint in a large bowl.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss.
Just before serving, add the crispy pita and sprinkle with the remaining [[1 tsp]] sumac.
Rinse the bulgur and soak it in the lemon juice for 20 minutes until softened.
Wash the parsley and mint well, then dry them completely with a towel or salad spinner. Wet herbs turn the salad soggy.
Chop the parsley very fine with a sharp knife and place it in a large bowl.
Add the mint, green onions and tomatoes.
Add the soaked bulgur with any lemon juice left in the bowl.
Add [[0.33 cup]] olive oil, [[1 tsp]] salt, [[0.25 tsp]] pepper and [[0.25 tsp]] allspice. Toss gently.
Taste and add more lemon or salt. Chill 15 minutes and serve with lettuce leaves.
Drain and rinse the chickpeas. Put them in a pot with water to cover and simmer for 20 minutes until very soft, for extra smooth hummus.
Whip [[0.5 cup]] tahini and [[0.25 cup]] lemon juice in a food processor for 1 minute until pale and thick.
Add the garlic, [[0.5 tsp]] cumin and [[0.75 tsp]] salt and blend 30 seconds.
Add half of the warm chickpeas and blend 1 minute. Add the rest and blend 2 minutes.
With the machine running, add [[4 tbsp]] ice water a spoonful at a time until creamy and light.
Spread in a shallow bowl, make a well in the center, and pour in [[2 tbsp]] olive oil.
Dust with [[0.5 tsp]] paprika, drizzle with the remaining [[1 tbsp]] oil, and serve with warm pita.
Toast [[1 cup]] walnuts in a dry skillet for 5 minutes over medium heat until fragrant. Cool slightly.
Pat the roasted peppers dry with paper towels.
Pulse the walnuts and [[0.5 cup]] breadcrumbs in a food processor until coarse crumbs.
Add the peppers, garlic, [[2 tbsp]] pomegranate molasses, [[1 tbsp]] lemon juice, [[1 tsp]] cumin, [[1 tsp]] Aleppo pepper and [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Blend while pouring in [[0.25 cup]] olive oil until the dip is thick and slightly rough.
Taste and adjust the salt, sweetness and heat. Chill for 30 minutes.
Serve with an olive oil drizzle, pita and raw vegetables.
Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C), or heat a gas burner or grill. Poke the eggplants a few times with a fork.
Roast the eggplants on a lined baking sheet for 45 minutes, turning halfway, until the skin is charred and the flesh collapses.
Cool them for 10 minutes, then slice open and scoop out the soft flesh. Discard the skins.
Drain the flesh in a sieve for 10 minutes, pressing out the bitter liquid.
Mash the flesh with a fork in a bowl.
Stir in [[0.25 cup]] tahini, [[3 tbsp]] lemon juice, the garlic and [[0.75 tsp]] salt.
Spread in a bowl, drizzle with [[2 tbsp]] olive oil and sprinkle with [[2 tbsp]] parsley. Serve with pita.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Bake the pita pieces on a sheet with [[1 tbsp]] melted butter for 8 minutes until crisp.
Mix [[2 cup]] yogurt, [[3 tbsp]] tahini, the garlic, [[2 tbsp]] lemon juice and [[0.5 tsp]] salt into a smooth sauce.
Drain the chickpeas, keeping a little liquid. Warm them in a pan with [[0.5 tsp]] cumin, [[0.5 tsp]] salt and a splash of liquid for 5 minutes.
Melt [[2 tbsp]] butter in a small pan. Toast the pine nuts for 3 minutes, stirring, until golden.
Layer the crisp pita in a serving dish. Top with the warm chickpeas.
Spoon the yogurt sauce over, then pour over the hot pine nut butter.
Sprinkle with [[0.5 tsp]] paprika and serve right away so the bread stays crisp.
Mix [[3 cup]] flour with [[0.5 tsp]] salt and about [[1 cup]] warm water. Knead for 8 minutes into a smooth dough. Rest 30 minutes.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a pan. Cook the onion for 4 minutes, add the lamb, [[0.5 tsp]] salt, [[0.5 tsp]] pepper and [[0.5 tsp]] allspice. Cook 8 minutes until no pink remains (160°F/71°C). Cool.
Roll the dough very thin and cut into 2 inch circles. Put a little filling on each and fold into half moons. Pinch the corners together to make small tortellini shapes.
Bake the dumplings on a sheet at 400°F (200°C) for 12 minutes until lightly golden.
Whisk the yogurt with [[1 tbsp]] cornstarch and the egg white in a pot. Heat over medium, stirring one way constantly, until it just comes to a boil. Simmer 8 minutes.
Fry the garlic with [[1 tsp]] dried mint in a little oil for 1 minute and stir into the yogurt with [[1 tsp]] salt.
Add the baked dumplings to the yogurt and simmer 5 minutes. Serve hot, sprinkled with the remaining [[2 tsp]] mint.
Rinse the bulgur, soak it in water for 15 minutes, then drain and squeeze dry.
Process the bulgur, grated onion, [[1 lb]] lamb, [[1 tsp]] allspice and [[1 tsp]] salt to a smooth paste. Chill 20 minutes.
Cook the diced onion in [[1 tbsp]] oil for 3 minutes, add [[0.25 lb]] lamb and cook 5 minutes until done (160°F/71°C). This is the filling.
Shape the paste into golf-ball-size balls, make a hole, fill with a little filling and close.
Whisk the yogurt with [[1 tbsp]] cornstarch in a large pot. Add [[0.25 cup]] rice and [[1 cup]] water. Heat on medium, stirring constantly, until it boils.
Reduce to low and simmer for 10 minutes. Add [[1 tsp]] salt.
Drop in the kibbeh balls and simmer gently for 20 minutes, until they float and are cooked through.
Fry the garlic with the mint in a little oil for 1 minute and stir it in. Serve hot.
Make the syrup: boil [[1 cup]] sugar, [[0.5 cup]] water and [[1 tsp]] lemon juice for 10 minutes. Stir in [[1 tsp]] rose water and cool.
Whisk the cream with [[2 tbsp]] sugar and [[1 tsp]] rose water in a cold bowl. Chill as the filling.
Bring [[2 cup]] water and [[0.5 cup]] sugar to a simmer. Whisk in [[0.75 cup]] semolina and cook, stirring, for 5 minutes until thick.
Add [[2 cup]] mozzarella and stir hard over low heat for 3 minutes until melted into a smooth stretchy dough.
Dust a board with [[2 tbsp]] powdered sugar. Spread the hot dough very thin into a rectangle about 8 x 12 inches. Cool for 15 minutes.
Spread a line of cream down one long side and roll up tightly like a log. Slice into 2 inch pieces.
Dip the ends in [[0.25 cup]] pistachios. Drizzle with the cooled syrup and serve chilled.
Make the syrup: simmer [[1.5 cup]] sugar, [[1 cup]] water and [[1 tbsp]] lemon juice for 10 minutes. Stir in [[1 tbsp]] rose water and cool completely.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Brush a 9 x 13 inch pan with melted butter.
Mix the chopped pistachios with [[2 tbsp]] sugar if you like it sweeter.
Lay a sheet of phyllo in the pan, brush with butter, and repeat until you have 10 sheets. Keep the stack covered with a damp towel.
Spread half of the pistachios on top. Add 5 more buttered sheets, then the rest of the pistachios.
Top with the remaining sheets, buttering each one, and brush the top with butter.
Cut into diamonds all the way through before baking. Bake for 45 minutes until deep golden.
Pour the cooled syrup over the hot baklava right away. Let it soak for at least 4 hours before serving.
